astra-6.text: The biggest cost is still the experimental validation. Computationally, you can generate and evaluate lots of nanobody candidates relatively cheaply. But then you have to make those molecules and test whether they actually bind to the target. That takes time and resources. So the value of the Virtual Lab is in helping us choose better candidates, so that each round of experiments is more informative.

sol-6.1.text: The biggest cost is still the experimental validation. The computational side—having the AI scientists discuss ideas, design nanobodies, and prioritize candidates—is relatively inexpensive. But once you have those candidates, you need to synthesize them, express the proteins, and run assays to see whether they actually bind. That’s where most of the money and time go. So a major goal of the Virtual Lab is to make those experiments more informative: choose better candidates so that you get more useful results from each round of testing.
